title: [FloodedRice/PerennialCropland report] Minor-season contributions added as raw w+wo sums instead of balance (w-wo)
description: In land.py:656-664 the minor-season loop builds a single minor_es list by appending both minor_calc.results_w and minor_calc.results_wo when the module has both is_with() and is_without() true. extract_emissions then sums them all positively. But the main module's emissions_set is a BALANCE list (w - wo, see api/calculators.py:407). Mixing raw w+wo contributions into a balance is unit-incorrect: the per-row breakdown (CO2 in biomass, CO2 in soils, etc.) gets inflated by the without-project gross emissions of every minor season. Same bug present in PerennialCroplandReport._add_minor_seasons.
acceptance_criteria: The contribution added for each minor season equals Result(minor_calc.results_w + minor_calc.results_start_w, minor_calc.results_wo + minor_calc.results_start_wo).balance — never raw w+wo concatenation. Verified by unit test with synthetic emission sets.
notes: Fix dovetails with Bug 2 — building per-season minor-balance and adding once is the natural shape.
close_reason: FloodedRice portion fixed in commit 97e56e70: each minor season's contribution is now Result(*).balance (w_full - wo_full), not raw with+without. PerennialCropland portion deferred to exact-django-webapp-flx (same bug pattern).

title: [FloodedRice/PerennialCropland report] Minor-season loop adds MAIN module start_w/wo, not minor's own start
description: djangoexact/api/reports/land.py:656-664 (FloodedRice) appends self.calculator.results_start_w and self.calculator.results_start_wo (i.e. the MAIN module's start emissions) once per minor season. Should be minor_calc.results_start_w / minor_calc.results_start_wo. With N minor seasons, the main module's start contribution gets added N extra times on top of what is already in emissions_set. PerennialCroplandReport at land.py:196-220 has a half-fixed mirror: its is_without branch correctly uses minor_calc.results_start_wo, but its is_with branch still uses self.calculator.results_start_w.
acceptance_criteria: No reference to self.calculator.results_start_w/wo inside the per-minor-season loop in either FloodedRiceReport or PerennialCroplandReport. With 2 minor seasons and a stale cache, total emissions reported equal the FloodedRiceCalculator total to within float epsilon.
notes: Pure copy-paste bug. Trivial fix once tested.
close_reason: FloodedRice portion fixed in commit 97e56e70: minor-season aggregation now uses minor_calc.results_start_w (via Result.balance) — never the main module's start. PerennialCropland portion deferred to exact-django-webapp-flx (same bug pattern; needs separate fix because PerennialCroplandCalculator doesn't aggregate minor seasons at all, unlike FloodedRiceCalculator).

title: [FloodedRice report] Report uses FloodedRiceSeasonCalculator (main only); production uses FloodedRiceCalculator (main + minors)
description: djangoexact/api/reports/land.py:634 sets self.calculator = FloodedRiceSeasonCalculator(self.module). CalculatorFactory().get_calculator() (api/calculators.py:463) resolves a FloodedRice instance to FloodedRiceCalculator (api/calculators.py:2891), which aggregates the main season AND every minor season. As a result, BaseModuleReport._init_from_calculator() runs the wrong calculator, and self.emissions_set is the main season alone unless the cache (populated by views.py via the FULL FloodedRiceCalculator) is valid. Module total _balance_total() therefore silently flips between correct (cache valid) and undercounted-by-minor-seasons (cache invalid) based on cache freshness.
acceptance_criteria: In both cache-valid and cache-invalid paths, BaseModuleReport.emissions_set for a FloodedRice module with N minor seasons equals the balance produced by FloodedRiceCalculator (main + all minor seasons).
notes: Likely fix: aggregate minor seasons into emissions_set/_w/_wo during __post_init__ (calculator path), making the cached and calculator paths produce the same shape.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 97e56e70: aggregation moved to FloodedRiceReport.__post_init__; stride-6 metadata helper; dead local removed; rows now consistent with module total in both cache and calculator paths. Tests in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py.

title: Flooded Rice (and Perennial Cropland) report numbers wrong, esp. with minor seasons
description: The Excel/HTML report for FloodedRice (and the mirror code in PerennialCroplandReport) produces incorrect per-row breakdowns and (under cache-stale conditions) incorrect module totals when the module has minor seasons. Root cause is a divergence between the report's own calculator (FloodedRiceSeasonCalculator, main season only) and the production CalculatorFactory path (FloodedRiceCalculator, main + all minor seasons), compounded by several copy-paste-style bugs in the in-report minor-season aggregation loop and the metadata layout. Six concrete defects are documented as child issues. See djangoexact/api/reports/land.py:629-723.
acceptance_criteria: All child bugs closed; FloodedRice (and PerennialCropland, where the same pattern exists) row sums == module total in the Excel report for projects with 0, 1, and 2+ minor seasons, in both cache-valid and cache-invalid states.
notes: Phase 1 investigation complete; pattern analysis + fixes pending. PerennialCroplandReport at land.py:196-220 shares the same bug pattern in a half-fixed form.
close_reason: FloodedRice portion fully resolved in commit 97e56e70 (closes 6 child bugs: h8z, ttm, fqg, 7qn, 65h, 7nt). PerennialCroplandReport has the same bug pattern but with different calculator semantics — separated to follow-up exact-django-webapp-flx. FloodedRice inventory items missing minor seasons separated to follow-up exact-django-webapp-80d. User's original symptom (flooded rice numbers in Excel report) is fixed.

title: Self-contained SQLite test bootstrap (run suite without cloud Postgres)
description: The unit suite has no fixture bootstrap and only ever ran against a pre-seeded Postgres (cloud-sql-proxy). bitbucket-pipelines.yml predeploy is a no-op (no CI test gate). Add: (1) settings.py SKIP_FIREBASE_INIT guard (Firebase block crashes at import without creds); (2) djangoexact/settings_test.py (sqlite + test secret + custom runner); (3) api/tests/runner.py SqliteReferenceTestRunner: load_reference_data --app=all + seed groups Admin/Second Reviewer/Staff (all perms) + canonical users testuser@example.com/test@user.org; (4) make migration 0286 vendor-aware (Postgres DO$$ block breaks sqlite migrate). Enables local validation of er8 refactor without Postgres.
notes: DONE & PROVEN: SQLite bootstrap works end-to-end. flooded_rice 6/6 PASS incl. test_patch__to_not_ready (er8 status path) + calculator/defaults. Pieces: settings.py SKIP_FIREBASE_INIT guard; settings_test.py; api/tests/runner.py + seed.py; setup_test_db cmd; admin_scripts SKIP_STARTUP_CATALOG_VALIDATION guard; migration 0286 vendor-aware; .gitignore test_db. Usage: manage.py setup_test_db --settings=djangoexact.settings_test ; manage.py test <targets> --settings=djangoexact.settings_test --keepdb. Broad 7-module gate: 33/67 fail but ALL triaged to pre-existing test brittleness (5l7 fixture gap; new factories-import/abstract-base bug) NOT er8/u7b.
close_reason: SQLite test bootstrap implemented and proven (flooded_rice 6/6 green incl. er8 status path). Remaining broad-gate failures triaged to pre-existing test brittleness, tracked separately.

title: Run unit suite in CI for status-validation refactor (er8) + verify behavioral nuances
description: exact-django-webapp-er8 was implemented but the dev sandbox has no Postgres/Docker, so the Django unit suite was not run locally. CI (or a DB-equipped machine) must run: python djangoexact/manage.py test api.tests.unit (focus: energy, settlement, irrigation, land_use_change, base_module, annual_cropland, forest_management, input, perennial_cropland, flooded_rice, grassland, coastal_wetland, storage, processing, packaging, transport). Verify the 3 documented intentional nuances do not break assertions: (1) cascade status persisted via QuerySet.update() -> no history/last_modified/lock-timestamp on cascade-target parents/LUC; (2) land-module create now recomputes status after save (previously always EMPTY) - check base_module create tests; (3) LandUseChange.get_modules() exception now caught -> EMPTY instead of 400. If any fail, the conditional-operator canonicalization (NoScenario used 'not get()' vs Scenario 'is None') and SUBMODULES_EMPTY precedence are the first suspects.
notes: SCOPED er8 validation done (local SQLite, branch vs pre-er8 develop baseline via worktree). 39/39 common status/cascade tests (test_modify=READY, test_patch_to_not_ready=EMPTY, test_parent_not_ready_if_submodule_not_ready=SUBMODULES_EMPTY cascade) pass IDENTICALLY on pre-er8 baseline (Ran 39 OK) and er8 branch -> status contract preserved across all module types. Step-4 er8-specific tests added & green: SUBMODULES_EMPTY-over-EMPTY precedence (settlement), conditional-field readiness (grassland), create-path READY (energy). REMAINING UNVALIDATED: LandUseChange calc/scenario tests, blocked by pre-existing non-er8 defects 4ng (auditlog x cached_results deepcopy) and 5gq (results-view get_object_or_404 query explosion). Recommend fixing 4ng/5gq then running api.tests.unit.land_use_change for full LUC coverage.

title: Report PDF 500: redundant nested flex in cover.html trips WeasyPrint skip_first_whitespace IndexError
description: GET /api/projects/<id>/report/ returns 500. WeasyPrint 68.0 raises IndexError in layout/inline.py:231 (skip_first_whitespace lacks an index>=len(children) bounds guard) when a nested flex column fragments across a page. Trigger isolated by bisection to reports/partials/{en,es,fr}/cover.html: the inner <div class='h-100 d-flex flex-column ...'> is byte-identical to its parent (redundant) and supplies the second flex level the bug needs. Also: the FAO logo asset is SVG (media/faologo_*.svg) but cover.html declares the data URI as image/eps — wrong MIME, logo cannot render. Fix: collapse the redundant nested flex div and correct MIME to image/svg+xml in all three cover templates.
close_reason: Collapsed redundant byte-identical nested flex div in en/es/fr cover.html (removed the 2nd flex level WeasyPrint 68.0 skip_first_whitespace IndexError needs) and corrected logo data-URI MIME image/eps->image/svg+xml. Verified: full real pipeline for project 937 now renders a 71KB PDF; previously 500'd.

title: Excel report under-counts: per-module report whitelists drop calculator emissions (Storage/Packaging Fuel, Settlement land)
description:
The refactored report package (api/reports/modules.py, land.py) computes each module's total_emissions and breakdown rows by extracting only a hardcoded whitelist of (ActivityType, GasType) pairs from the module's balance, silently dropping every other category the calculator emits.

Proven from project 'test may 2026' embedded module caches (no DB needed, see _repro_report_bug.py):
- Downstream correct=-47148.10 (matches expected -47148); report yields +12457.
  - StorageReport extracts only STORAGE+ELECTRICITY -> drops Fuel CO2/N2O = -66236.35
  - PackagingReport extracts only PACKAGING+ELECTRICITY -> drops Fuel CO2/CH4/N2O = +6631.72
- New facilities: Settlement full balance=108425.45 (matches expected 108425); SettlementReport extracts only ROADS/buildings/infra and hardcodes the 5 land rows to zeros -> drops Soil CO2 Change 365.61 + Soil Organic Matter N2O 22.84.

Regression introduced when feature/scenario-builder-per-change-units (#166) split a separate 'Fuel' activity out of value-chain modules; report whitelists were never updated. Pre-refactor project aggregate captured all emissions because it summed by GAS type over the full balance.

Acceptance: report's per-module total equals the full sum of that module's emissions_set; Downstream activity total = -47148, Settlement module total = 108425 for this project; no emission category silently dropped; regression test using embedded cache fixture.
notes:
FIX IMPLEMENTED & VERIFIED (offline, against project 'test may 2026' embedded module caches using the REAL api.reports.extractors.extract_emissions):
- Downstream activity total: 12456.54 -> -47148.10 (expected -47148) PASS
- New facilities / Settlement module: 108037.00 -> 108425.45 (expected 108425) PASS
- Project-wide regression guard: _balance_total() byte-identical to old per-module total for ALL already-correct modules across all 13 activities; only Storage(+6631.72 Fuel), Packaging(... Fuel), Settlement(+388.45 land) changed.
Changes: base.py BaseModuleReport._balance_total(); all module compute() use it for total_emissions; Storage/Packaging derive rows from module balance and add N2O/CH4/CO2-from-fuel rows; Settlement restores 5 land rows via _extract_land_base(). Regression unit test added: api/tests/reports/test_cache.py::TestBalanceTotalIncludesAllActivities (DB-free; arithmetic validated against real extractor). Note: Django test runner not runnable in this env (no firebase_admin/Postgres) — run 'python manage.py test api.tests.reports.test_cache' in CI. OrganicSoilReport intentionally left at zeros (emissions attributed to its LandUseChange; full-sum would double count).
close_reason: Root cause found, fixed and verified offline against real project export; committed 87cdc6b8 and pushed to develop. Follow-ups filed for the 3 secondary findings.

title: Perennial biomass: agb_maximum_c_tier_2=0 discarded by truthiness check
description: In djangoexact/math_model/no_time_dependency_final/perennial_cropping.py lines 171 & 177, calculate_biomass_emissions uses 'if self.agb_maximum_c_tier_2:' (truthiness). A user-supplied 0.0 is falsy, so it is treated as 'not provided' and replaced by the tier-1 default self.agb_maximum_c. Workaround value 1e-10 is truthy so it survives, hence '0 wrong, 0.0000000001 right'. Field is models.FloatField(null=True) and dataclass agb_maximum_c_tier_2: Optional[float]=None, so None=not provided and 0.0=explicit zero are distinct. Rest of same file (lines 67-94,167-168) correctly uses 'is None'. Secondary same-class bug at calculators.py:1935-1937 ('getattr(...) or self.parent...') affects minor-season propagation.
notes: Fixed in perennial_cropping.py calculate_biomass_emissions: introduced cap_provided = (agb_maximum_c_tier_2 is not None) and capped = cap_provided or max_agb != 0. Explicit 0.0 now honoured as a real zero cap (matches the 1e-10 workaround, biomass CO2 -> ~0); None still falls back to tier-1 default; positive caps unchanged. Regression: djangoexact/scripts/repro_perennial_agb_max_zero.py (FAIL before, PASS after). REMAINING: sibling antipattern at calculators.py:1935-1937 ('getattr(...) or self.parent...') still drops a 0 for minor-season perennials whose parent differs - out of scope for this fix, see follow-up.
close_reason: Root cause (truthiness check discarding explicit 0.0) fixed and verified with regression script

title: Patch pip-audit CVEs: bump Django 5.2.13→5.2.14, urllib3 2.6.3→2.7.0
description: pip-audit on djangoexact/requirements.txt reports 5 known CVEs: Django 5.2.13 has CVE-2026-35192, CVE-2026-6907, CVE-2026-5766 (fixed in 5.2.14). urllib3 2.6.3 has CVE-2026-44431, CVE-2026-44432 (fixed in 2.7.0). Bump pinned versions in requirements.txt and re-run pip-audit to confirm clean.
close_reason: Bumped Django to 5.2.14 and urllib3 to 2.7.0; pip-audit --strict reports no known vulnerabilities.

title: Debug: /enqueue-job fails with Read-only file system /workspace/logs in review
description: When calling htmx_enqueue_job in the review env, the request fails with: Read-only file system: '/workspace/logs'. /workspace is the read-only deployed source bundle on Cloud Run/GAE; only /tmp is writable. Need to find what code path writes there and either redirect to a writable location or guard it for read-only deployments.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: review runs on App Engine Standard (Python 3.11 per djangoexact/app.yaml) where the filesystem is read-only except /tmp. admin_scripts/job_dispatcher.py:dispatch_job branches on CLOUD_RUN_COMPUTATION_JOB_NAME — empty in review (not in app.yaml env_variables) — and falls into the local-dev subprocess path that does (BASE_DIR/'logs').mkdir() on /workspace/logs → Read-only file system: '/workspace/logs'.

FIX (both layers, per user direction):
1) Code (job_dispatcher.py:97-108): respect EXACT_JOB_LOG_DIR env override; default to BASE_DIR/logs; on OSError fall back to tempfile.gettempdir()/exact_job_logs. Added imports tempfile + pathlib.Path.
2) Config (app.yaml): added CLOUD_RUN_COMPUTATION_JOB_NAME and CLOUD_RUN_REGION as substitution placeholders so once a Cloud Run Job is provisioned, the deploy pipeline injects the resource path and the dispatcher takes the proper Cloud Run path.

REMAINING ARCHITECTURAL GAP (not in scope of this fix): until a Cloud Run Job is provisioned and CLOUD_RUN_COMPUTATION_JOB_NAME is set in CI/CD, review still falls into subprocess. Subprocess on GAE Standard is unlikely to survive past the request lifetime — /enqueue-job will return 200 cleanly but the spawned process will likely be killed when the instance scales. Provision Cloud Run Job + wire the env var to fully fix execution.
close_reason: Code + config fix shipped on develop (commit 87d9fac1). Hardened job_dispatcher to fall back to tempfile.gettempdir()/exact_job_logs when BASE_DIR/logs is read-only; added CLOUD_RUN_COMPUTATION_JOB_NAME and CLOUD_RUN_REGION placeholders to app.yaml. Verification pending review-env deploy. Follow-up needed: provision Cloud Run Job for review and wire its resource name into CI/CD substitution so dispatch routes through Cloud Run Jobs (subprocess fallback won't survive on GAE Standard even with the log-dir fix). Reopen if /enqueue-job still errors after deploy.

title: Debug: minitool_changerecord table missing in tunneled environment
description: When calling /api/admin-scripts/compile-scenarios/htmx/run-scenario/ in the online tool, PostgreSQL returns: relation "minitool_changerecord" does not exist. Query is MAX("minitool_changerecord"."total") AS "maxv" from scenario_utils.stats_for(). User is connected to the failing environment via tunnel. Need to determine if (a) migrations not applied, (b) connected to wrong database/schema, or (c) table dropped. Investigate root cause before fixing.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED via tunneled review DB (localhost:5432, db=exact, user=exact_user, PG 14.22):

EVIDENCE:
- Zero minitool_* tables exist (information_schema.tables LIKE 'minitool_%' returns 0 rows)
- django_migrations on this DB records ALL 27 minitool migrations as applied (latest 0027 on 2025-10-20 15:17 UTC)
- django_content_type has 17 minitool ContentType rows; auth_permission has 68 perms referencing them
- No FKs from other apps point into minitool_* tables (cross-app safe)
- Other apps (api, ipcc, admin_scripts, auditlog) have their tables intact

HISTORICAL CONTEXT (git):
- Until commit a02a64bc (2026-04-16, 'feat(minitool): remove sqlite DB alias and router') the minitool app was routed to a separate sqlite 'minitool' DB alias via minitool/db_router.py. allow_migrate returned True only for db=='minitool', so default (Postgres) never had minitool tables created.
- After a02a64bc, develop expects minitool to use default Postgres. But review's default DB still has the stale ledger entries (presumably set via --fake at some point) and 0 actual tables.

PATTERN:
- Classic 'django_migrations recorded but tables missing' = fake-applied migration history.

FIX (reversible, no data loss because tables are empty/absent):
1. Snapshot stale rows: SELECT * FROM django_migrations WHERE app='minitool';
2. python manage.py migrate minitool zero --fake   (removes ledger rows; no DDL since tables don't exist)
3. python manage.py migrate minitool   (creates all 27 migrations' DDL for real)
4. ContentType/Permission rows are reused (Django doesn't duplicate)

Pending user approval before executing against shared review env.
close_reason: Recovered review DB. ROOT CAUSE: stale django_migrations ledger entries (27 fake-applied rows) on default Postgres after sqlite minitool DB alias was removed in commit a02a64bc — actual minitool_* tables never existed in default DB. FIX (against tunneled review DB on localhost:5432): 1) snapshot stale rows; 2) python manage.py migrate minitool zero --fake (cleared ledger, no DDL); 3) python manage.py migrate minitool (created all 7 tables for real). Verified: 7 minitool_* tables present, original failing query 'SELECT MAX("minitool_changerecord"."total")...' succeeds (returns NULL on empty table). Tables are empty — review env may need import_all_changes/scenario data import for /run-scenario to return non-empty stats.

title: Restructure scenario filters: global=region, per-change=climate/moisture/soil_type
description: The per-change Region and Climate dropdowns inside Change-level Filters render as empty <select> elements on initial page load — same root cause as the global region filter fixed in 28dd1c12. change_fieldset.html has no <option> loop and no view (compile_scenarios, htmx_add_change, htmx_add_scenario) passes regions/climates to the template context. Only htmx_filters populates them after module_type is picked, which is module-scoped and deferred, leaving the dropdowns blank to the user.
notes: Originally scoped to populating empty per-change region/climate dropdowns (same root cause as 28dd1c12). Expanded mid-task: per-change filter set restructured to climate+moisture+soil_type (3-col grid); global filter reduced to region only (soil_type dropped, no more hardcoded default selection). POST parsing, htmx_filters endpoint, and tests updated to match.

title: [ForestManagementReport] Disturbance metadata layout: label/data row mismatch, stride-1 collision, and degradation row overlaps disturbances
description: api/reports/land.py:939-958 has three overlapping issues in the per-disturbance metadata block: (1) Label/data row mismatch: row 17+i col=1 is labeled 'Disturbance X: type' but no col=2/3/4 value is written on that row; row 18+i col=1 is labeled 'distrubance recurrence (years)' (sic, typo) but the col=2/3/4 value on that row is dist.disturbance_type.name — labels are off by one relative to data. (2) Stride-1 collision: with 2+ disturbances, header rows (17+i, 18+i, 19+i) and data rows (18+i, 19+i, 20+i) all collide between consecutive disturbances. Same bug class as 65h / 5g2. (3) Degradation row overlap: deg_row = 17 + len(disturbances) (line 953) places the 'average yearly degradation (%)' row at row 17+N, which collides with the disturbance block's last row for N >= 1 (e.g. with 1 disturbance, deg_row = 18 which is already used by disturbance i=0; with 2 disturbances, deg_row = 19 used by disturbance i=1's data). Also has a cosmetic typo: 'distrubance' should be 'disturbance'.
acceptance_criteria: For any number of disturbances N >= 0, the (row_offset, col) coordinates of every MetadataWrite in ForestManagementReport.compute are unique AND each col=1 label matches the field whose value is written on the same row at col >= 2. Degradation row does not overlap any disturbance row. Typo 'distrubance' corrected to 'disturbance'.
notes: Discovered during follow-up audit after the FloodedRice fix (epic exact-django-webapp-i6i). Same bug class as 65h (FloodedRice) and 5g2 (Energy). Most ForestManagement projects probably use 0 or 1 disturbance, masking the multi-disturbance collisions; the label/data mismatch and degradation overlap are visible even with 1 disturbance.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 79c91274: new _forest_disturbance_metadata_writes helper emits stride-3 per disturbance with col=1 labels aligned to col >= 2 data on the same row. ForestManagementReport.compute uses base_row = 17 + 3 * i; deg_row = 17 + 3 * len(disturbances). Typo 'distrubance' corrected. Tests in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py (TestForestDisturbanceMetadata, 5 tests).

title: [EnergyReport] Per-electricity and per-fuel metadata row offsets collide for 2+ entries (stride 1 vs 4)
description: api/reports/modules.py:495-526 writes 4 metadata rows per electricity entry at offsets (i, 1+i, 2+i, 3+i) for fields (country, grid MWh, renewable MWh, EF scope). With 2+ electricities, season i=1 writes rows 1, 2, 3, 4 — which collide with i=0's rows 1, 2, 3 (only the last write wins). Same pattern at lines 530-560 for fuels: offsets (fuel_base+i, fuel_base+1+i, fuel_base+2+i, fuel_base+3+i) collide for 2+ fuels. For single-electricity / single-fuel modules (the most common case) there is no visible collision, which is why this has been latent. Stride should be 4: i.e. 4*i + 0, 4*i + 1, 4*i + 2, 4*i + 3. Same bug class as exact-django-webapp-65h (FloodedRice metadata stride 6).
acceptance_criteria: For any number of electricities N >= 1 and fuels M >= 1, the (row_offset, col) coordinates of all MetadataWrite entries in the Energy metadata block are unique. Asserted by a unit test mirroring TestMinorSeasonMetadataStride in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py.
notes: Discovered during follow-up audit after the FloodedRice fix (epic exact-django-webapp-i6i). Same bug class as 65h. Cheapest fix is to extract a small helper similar to _flooded_rice_minor_season_metadata_writes for each entry kind.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 79c91274: new _energy_electricity_metadata_writes and _energy_fuel_metadata_writes helpers emit stride-4 blocks per entry. EnergyReport.compute uses base_row = 4 * index; fuel_base = 4 * len(electricities). Tests in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py (TestEnergyMetadataStride, 5 tests).

title: [PerennialCropland + AnnualCropland reports] Same minor-season aggregation bugs as FloodedRice (filed under ttm + fqg) — fix similarly
description: PerennialCroplandReport._add_minor_seasons (api/reports/land.py:196-220) AND AnnualCroplandReport._add_minor_seasons (api/reports/land.py:298-319) carry the same two bug patterns as the FloodedRice loop fixed in epic exact-django-webapp-i6i: (1) the is_with branch (and, in AnnualCropland, also the is_without branch) appends self.calculator.results_start_w/wo (the MAIN module's start) instead of minor_calc.results_start_w/wo — see exact-django-webapp-ttm. PerennialCropland is half-fixed (its is_without branch correctly uses minor_calc.results_start_wo); AnnualCropland has both branches broken. (2) both append raw minor.results_w + minor.results_wo to a single minor_es list, then sum positively via extract_emissions — yielding a gross sum rather than a balance and mixing units with the main module's emissions_set which is a (w - wo) balance (see exact-django-webapp-fqg). Both modules also share the cache-divergence problem (h8z-style): PerennialCroplandCalculator (calculators.py:2489) and AnnualCroplandCalculator (calculators.py:1888) are pass-throughs of PerennialCropCalculator / AnnualCropCalculator, neither of which iterates minor seasons. So in BOTH the API /results cache (populated via CalculatorFactory) AND the report calculator path, only main-season emissions are present unless the in-report loop runs — and that loop is broken. Likely fix: mirror the FloodedRice approach in BOTH reports (extract a _aggregate_minor_seasons_into_emissions_sets-style helper, merge into emissions_set in __post_init__, drop the in-compute loop). Also drop the dead total_emissions local in compute() in both (see 7nt-style cleanup).
acceptance_criteria: PerennialCroplandReport produces correct numbers (rows add up to module total) with 0, 1, and 2+ minor seasons. _add_minor_seasons removed from compute(); minor seasons aggregated into emissions_set in __post_init__.
notes: Follows the FloodedRice pattern closed under epic exact-django-webapp-i6i. Originally scoped to PerennialCropland only; AnnualCropland added during follow-up audit since it shares identical calculator semantics and bug pattern. Both should be fixed with the same helper signature, ideally in a single PR.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 79c91274: PerennialCroplandReport and AnnualCroplandReport now use the generic _aggregate_minor_seasons_into_emissions_sets helper (parameterized by calculator class). _add_minor_seasons removed; minor seasons aggregated into emissions_set in __post_init__; minor inventories also merged via _merge_minor_inventories. Tests in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py (TestAggregateMinorSeasonsIntoEmissionsSets).

title: [FloodedRice report] Minor-season metadata row offsets collide (stride should be 6, not 1)
description: djangoexact/api/reports/land.py:700-707 writes 6 metadata rows per minor season at offsets 8+i, 9+i, 10+i, 11+i, 12+i, 13+i. For i=0 that is rows 8..13 (area, cultivation_period, before, after, organic, yield); for i=1 it is rows 9..14, which collide with i=0's rows 9..13. Last write wins, so with 2+ minor seasons the metadata block is silently corrupt. Stride should be 6: 8+6*i, 9+6*i, ..., 13+6*i.
acceptance_criteria: For any number of minor seasons N, the (row, col) coordinates of all MetadataWrite entries are unique. Asserted by unit test.
notes: Pure indexing bug. One-line fix in the offset expressions.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 97e56e70: aggregation moved to FloodedRiceReport.__post_init__; stride-6 metadata helper; dead local removed; rows now consistent with module total in both cache and calculator paths. Tests in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py.

title: [FloodedRice report] fire_ch4 not updated in minor-season loop

The 'CH4 from fires' result row for FloodedRice modules with minor seasons therefore shows only the main season's STRAW_BURNING CH4, while _balance_total() (the module total) does include it under cache-valid conditions. Rows do not add up to total.
acceptance_criteria: With 1+ minor season(s), the 'CH4 from fires' row value equals the sum of STRAW_BURNING CH4 across main + every minor season. Asserted by unit test.
notes: Trivial omission. Add the fire_ch4 _add(...) line analogous to fire_n2o.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 97e56e70: aggregation moved to FloodedRiceReport.__post_init__; stride-6 metadata helper; dead local removed; rows now consistent with module total in both cache and calculator paths. Tests in api/tests/reports/test_flooded_rice_seasons.py.

title: Expose granular readiness payload on module detail endpoints
description: Surface the per-scenario missing-field codes and blocking-children references that compute_readiness already produces, as an additive readiness object on every module detail GET/PATCH/POST response. Status FK shape unchanged; list endpoints unchanged (thin-list contract preserved). Builds on the er8 refactor (ReadinessMixin.compute_readiness). Frontend will use the structured codes to render per-field 'required' highlights on the module edit form and a banner-level summary composed from its own i18n catalog (backend stays language-neutral).
design: Hybrid approach: api/models.py.ReadinessMixin.compute_readiness returns structured code dicts instead of strings; new ReadinessMixin.get_blocking_children method; new api/readiness.py builds the response dict via build_readiness_payload(); BaseGenericModuleSerializer gets a ReadinessSerializerMixin adding readiness = SerializerMethodField. Backend fully language-neutral. Spec at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-20-granular-readiness-payload-design.md.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/<module>/<id>/ returns readiness object with shape {missing: {start: [{field, reason, trigger?}], with: [], without: []}, blocking_children: [{id, type, status}]}; list endpoints unchanged; existing status assertions in unit tests still pass; new test_readiness.py covers all branches; FE can render per-field highlights using the codes alone.

title: results view get_object_or_404 query-compilation explosion on LUC-linked modules (effective hang)
description: Pre-existing, NOT er8 (pure read path, predates refactor, untouched by status changes). In api/views.py:2412 GenericModuleViewSet.results -> get_object_or_404(model, pk=pk), Django's SQL compiler is stuck in get_select/build_filter/setup_query forever (~0 useful CPU over ~1h, two faulthandler dumps both in query compilation, then Windows access violation = memory thrash) when the module participates in a LandUseChange scenario (AnnualToForestTestCase etc.). Signature = explosive/recursive query construction (likely select_related/prefetch over the LandModule<->LandUseChange OneToOne cycle, or a default-manager queryset). Only surfaced once exact-django-webapp-8ae factory fix let LUC calc tests run. Blocks all api.tests.unit.land_use_change(_examples) tests -> excluded from the scoped er8 validation. Prod impact: potential pathological latency on the module results endpoint for LUC-linked modules. Repro: python djangoexact/manage.py test api.tests.unit.land_use_change.AnnualToForestTestCase.test_annual_to_forest_calculation --settings=djangoexact.settings_test --keepdb (hangs at get_module_results).

title: auditlog audits multi-MB cached_results_* JSON on every module save (AUDITLOG_INCLUDE_ALL_MODELS=True)
description: Pre-existing, NOT er8-caused (er8 cascade uses .update() which bypasses post_save/auditlog; old code did MORE audited saves). AUDITLOG_INCLUDE_ALL_MODELS=True auto-registers every model incl CachedResultMixin module models. On each module.save() the post_save receiver (auditlog/receivers.py:40 log_create -> _create_log_entry) creates a LogEntry whose JSONField deepcopies all changed fields, including cached_results_total/by_activity/by_gas/by_activity_by_gas (multi-MB after a LUC calculation). copy.deepcopy of that nested blob thrashes (~0 CPU, ~hr, Windows access violation) -> effectively hangs the LUC calculation tests. Surfaced once exact-django-webapp-8ae factory fix let LUC calc tests actually run. Prod impact: every cache write audit-logs huge JSON -> auditlog_logentry table bloat + save latency. Fix options: AUDITLOG_EXCLUDE_TRACKING_FIELDS add cached_results_*/cached_units_breakdown (or exclude CachedResultMixin models from auditing), or wrap cache_results() in auditlog.context.disable_auditlog(). Tests neutralize via settings_test AUDITLOG_INCLUDE_ALL_MODELS=False.

title: er8 perf: eliminate redundant second readiness recompute per write (double is_start/with/without)
description: Status/readiness is computed twice per module write: (1) BaseModuleSerializer/BaseSubmoduleSerializer.validate -> recompute_status(persist=False) sets data[status] (DRF then persists it); (2) save() -> recompute_with_dependents -> instance.recompute_status(persist=False? no persist=True) recomputes the SAME value again + drives the cascade. Pass 2's self-recompute is redundant on the API path (idempotent) and doubles the is_start/is_with/is_without DEBUG logging + scenario-predicate queries. Fix: add recompute_self flag to recompute_with_dependents; serializer save() passes recompute_self=False (instance status already computed in validate & persisted by DRF); dependents still recomputed. External callers keep default True. Serves er8 'speed and simplicity'.
close_reason: Implemented recompute_self flag; serializer save() passes recompute_self=False. Verified SQLite gate: single readiness pass per write, cascade dependents preserved (test_parent_not_ready_if_submodule_not_ready passes), no regression (failures 10->6, errors 18->17, -26% runtime).

title: Pre-existing test brittleness: wrong factories import module + abstract base TestCases collected
description: Surfaced by the SQLite suite run (NOT caused by er8 or u7b). title: Refactor Module/Submodule status validation to model layer
description: Replace 3 duplicate serializer is_ready engines + 13 hardcoded SUBMODULES_EMPTY blocks + serializer-reinstantiation cascade with: one model-layer compute_readiness engine driven by a READINESS_CONFIG registry, a generic recompute_status (incl. SUBMODULES_EMPTY rule), a cached status_type_id resolver, and a declarative DEPENDENCY_MAP cascade via recompute_with_dependents. Internal redesign only: same API output and status strings, no DB migration, existing tests must pass. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/analyze-the-whole-module-enchanted-abelson.md
notes: Implemented (Steps 1-7). models.py: StatusNames, cached status_type_id/status_type, READINESS_CONFIG/READINESS_SCENARIO_GATED/DEPENDENCY_MAP registries, ReadinessMixin(compute_readiness/recompute_status/_has_unready_submodules/_extra_submodules_for_status), recompute_with_dependents (FIFO BFS), LandUseChange.recompute_status + Energy._extra_submodules_for_status overrides, _register_default_dependents. serializers.py: 3 is_ready engines + abstract collapsed to one model-delegating engine; 13 hardcoded SUBMODULES_EMPTY blocks removed (generic via _has_unready_submodules, SUBMODULES_EMPTY now takes precedence over EMPTY to match old early-return/override-after-super behavior); parent_validation + LandModuleSeralizer side-effects + LUC re-serialization removed, cascade now via recompute_with_dependents in Base*Serializer.save. NO DB in sandbox -> not run locally; CI is the validation gate (py_compile passes for all touched files). Known intentional nuances: (1) cascade status persistence uses .update() so no extra history/last_modified/lock-timestamp for cascade-target parents/LUC; (2) land-module create now recomputes status post-save (was always EMPTY before) - only differs for create-with-full-payload; (3) LandUseChange.get_modules() exception now caught -> LUC EMPTY instead of propagating 400.
close_reason: Implementation complete (models.py + serializers.py, py_compile clean). CI validation tracked by exact-django-webapp-cgj which depends on this.

title: Result.__add__ appends non-overlapping entries by reference (aliasing risk, not a copy)
description: math_model/no_time_dependency_final/ghg_emissions_classes.py Result.__add__ (line ~236): the no-match branch does result_obj.yearly_emissions_by_sector_by_gas.append(other_yearly_emission) — appends the OTHER Result's YearlyGasActivityEmissionSet by reference rather than a deepcopy. result_obj is a deepcopy of self, but entries unique to  are shared. If a source Result is added into multiple targets and subsequently mutated (e.g. reused accumulator, in-place emission edits), the shared reference can cross-contaminate / double-apply. Not the active cause of the report under-count or the Settlement double (those are fixed), but a latent correctness hazard. Recommend appending copy.deepcopy(other_yearly_emission) (mirror __sub__ which constructs a fresh YearlyGasActivityEmissionSet). Add a unit test that mutates a shared source after addition.

title: Verify LandUseChange + destination land module accounting vs the online EX-ACT tool (possible methodological double-count)
description: Activities pairing a LandUseChange module with a destination land module (project 'test may 2026': 'new agroforestry'=PerennialCropland+Grassland+LandUseChange; 'Deforestation'=AnnualCropland+ForestManagement+LandUseChange; 'New facilities'=Settlement+SetAside+LandUseChange) have their activity total = sum of ALL module balances. Whether the one-time transition stock change (LandUseChange) and the destination land dynamics should both be summed, or netted, is an EX-ACT methodology question. The webapp sums them; if the online tool nets/handles transitions differently the totals diverge BY DESIGN (not a code x+=x bug). This is the most likely remaining source of 'general' divergence the user observed. ACTION: compare one such activity (e.g. Deforestation) module-by-module against the online tool to determine whether the webapp's per-module summation matches the reference methodology; only change logic with domain confirmation. No code change made unilaterally.

title: SettlementCalculator possible double-add: self.results_w += self.results_w
description: api/calculators.py SettlementCalculator.calculate() ~line 4625 does 'self.results_w += self.results_w' / 'self.results_wo += self.results_wo' which doubles the accumulated results before adding building/road submodules. Verify this is intentional; if a bug it inflates Settlement land emissions consistently in both cached and recalculated paths (so it did not affect the report-layer fix in exact-django-webapp-jcb, but may make absolute Settlement numbers wrong vs the canonical EX-ACT tool).
close_reason: CONFIRMED double-count and FIXED. calculators.py SettlementCalculator.calculate() did 'self.results_w += self.results_w' / '_wo += _wo' (calculators.py:4621-4622), doubling ALL Settlement land + start-scenario emissions (buildings/roads added afterward were NOT doubled). Result.__add__ element-wise sums matching (year,gas,activity) entries, so x+=x is a literal x2. Every sibling land calculator single-counts via 'results_w + results_start_w' (e.g. lines 1885,2484,2886,3185); Settlement was the only one with the self-add. Removed the 2 lines; Settlement now = (math_w + start_w) + buildings + roads, matching siblings. NOTE: the embedded .exactp module caches were produced by the buggy calculator (doubled); offline regen cannot un-double them — the fix applies when the calculator recomputes (cache miss) in the running app/CI.

title: Refactor stats_for to use statistics.stdev and consistent quantile method

title: Staff Group with full admin permissions
description: Replace the previous per-user post_save permission grant with a maintained Group called 'Staff' that holds every Permission. A post_migrate handler ensures the Group exists and its permissions stay in sync with Permission.objects.all() (so newly-created permissions from future migrations propagate). A post_save handler on CustomUser adds is_staff=True users to the Staff Group and removes is_staff=False users from it, so group membership tracks is_staff bidirectionally. Cleaner and more reversible than per-user grants — edit the Group later to scope back, and group membership is visible/auditable in the admin.
close_reason: Closed

title: Auto-grant all permissions to staff users on save
description: Staff users (is_staff=True) currently log into the Django admin but see an empty interface because they have no model permissions granted. They need explicit user_permissions or group memberships, otherwise the admin sidebar shows nothing. User intent: any is_staff=True user should be able to use the admin freely (all apps, all models, including auth/sessions). Solution: post_save signal on CustomUser that sets user_permissions to Permission.objects.all() when is_staff=True and not is_superuser. Also a post_migrate signal so newly created Permissions (from future migrations) propagate to existing staff users.
notes:
Implemented via two signal handlers in djangoexact/api/signals.py:

1. post_save on CustomUser: when is_staff=True and not is_superuser, sets user_permissions to Permission.objects.all(). Fires on every staff user save (create or update), so promoting any user to staff immediately grants full admin.

2. post_migrate (global, no sender filter): iterates all is_staff=True, is_superuser=False users and re-syncs their user_permissions. Ensures existing staff users get permissions for NEW models added in future migrations. Also serves as the backfill mechanism for currently-existing staff users — they will get full perms on the next deploy when migrate runs.

Auto-wired via existing api/apps.py ready() pattern (imports signals, which triggers @receiver decorators). No apps.py changes needed.

Note: cannot run the test suite locally (postgres auth failing in dev env). signals.py byte-compiles clean. Existing admin_scripts tests create is_staff=True users but make no permission assertions, so the auto-grant won't break them.
close_reason: Closed

title: [FloodedRice report] Inventory items don't include minor-season contributions

notes: Filed as follow-up while fixing the emissions-aggregation bugs in epic exact-django-webapp-i6i. Not in scope for that epic.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 79c91274: _aggregate_minor_seasons_into_emissions_sets now also collects each minor season's calculator.inventory; new _merge_minor_inventories helper aggregates them with the main inventory via Inventory.__add__ (sums by gas_type+activity, appends new keys). FloodedRice, PerennialCropland, and AnnualCropland reports all assign the merged inventory to self.inventory before save_results_to_cache fires. title: [reports] Drop dead local total_emissions / total in compute() methods after 87cdc6b8 migration
description: Commit 87cdc6b8 migrated every per-module report to use ModuleResult.total_emissions=self._balance_total() (the full module balance) instead of the locally-computed total_emissions sum. The local variables were left dangling and are now dead code in many modules — misleading for readers and partially masking the row-vs-total divergence that the FloodedRice fix uncovered (see exact-django-webapp-7nt). Confirmed dead locals in: LandUseChangeReport (land.py:139), PerennialCroplandReport (line 228), AnnualCroplandReport (line 327), SetAsideReport (line 417), GrasslandReport (line 457), OtherLandReport (line 528), CoastalWetlandReport (line 561), and several non-land reports in modules.py (lines 105, 164, 350, 483, 622, 716, 972, 1040 — local 'total'). FloodedRice's dead local has already been removed; ForestManagement's local 'total_emissions' was renamed to be reused, verify if still needed. The PerennialCropland + AnnualCropland locals will likely be removed by exact-django-webapp-flx's fix; the rest of land.py + modules.py is pure cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: No compute() method computes a local total_emissions / total that is then not used anywhere. PR is mechanical and DB-free testable via test_cache.py-style assertions on extract_emissions output.

description: djangoexact/api/reports/land.py:672 computes 'total_emissions = _add(_add(...))' from the per-row local sums, but the value returned in the ModuleResult on line 717 is self._balance_total() (set by fix exact-django-webapp-jcb / commit 87cdc6b8). title: scenario-builder: decide raw-vs-coerced units in Excel export Changes sheet
description: compile_scenarios_export writes change.get('unit', '') (raw POSTed string) into the Units column of the Changes sheet. A user posting garbage like 'abc' would see 'abc' in the Changes sheet while the Summary sheet silently uses 1.0 (via _coerce_unit). Decide: (a) keep raw to reflect user input verbatim, or (b) write _coerce_unit(change.get('unit')) for self-consistency between the two sheets. Document the decision; update views.py compile_scenarios_export if (b).

title: scenario-builder: regression-guard test for Units input surviving HTMX swap
description: The Units input in change_fieldset.html is placed outside both HTMX swap targets (-field-container, -values-container) so changing module_type or field cannot clobber a typed unit value. This is correct by construction but untested. Add a test asserting the Units input is rendered outside both swap-target divs, so a future template restructure that moves it inside one of them is caught. Suggested location: admin_scripts/tests/test_views.py CompileScenariosViewTest.
